one_line: Human-authorized endpoint policy change lab with agent investigation and staged remediation.
what_it_does: Models a device fleet, exposes structured inspection/simulation/staging/apply/rollback actions, and keeps human authorization and audit state in the same dashboard.
leverage_rationale: Structured fleet state, blast-radius simulation, staged changes, authorization, and rollback make the agent materially more reliable than UI-driving automation for endpoint policy work.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe shared React state and domain logic for UI and WebMCP tools.
Claimed workflow includes affected-device inspection, impact simulation, staging, human authorization, apply, audit, and rollback.
Frame sheet visibly shows an operations dashboard and managed-device inventory, though not every agent action is legible.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent operations product with multiple aligned surfaces and a realistic deterministic fleet model, but the absence of video and limited readable frame detail caps end-to-end confidence.
execution_evidence: FACTS report a live demo and 11 gallery images.
Frame sheet shows dashboard metrics, health visualizations, managed-device table, and activity/status panels.
About text specifies devices, groups, policies, conflicts, staged changes, and audit events.
impact_rationale: Endpoint administrators have a concrete high-stakes need to understand policy conflicts and blast radius before making fleet changes; the human approval boundary directly addresses operational risk.
impact_evidence: About text identifies overlapping assignments, affected devices, exceptions, and side effects as the target problem.
Product keeps execution behind explicit human authorization and supports rollback.
creativity_rationale: The agent-native change lab and explicit prepare-authorize-execute model are a thoughtful synthesis for endpoint operations, though the underlying domain is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent analyzes and stages remediation rather than receiving unrestricted write access.
Shared live dashboard and authorization handoff are central to the concept.
usability_note: Dashboard and managed-device views appear organized and operationally legible; exact interaction quality is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; frame sheets are repetitive and low-resolution.
Several metric labels and exact end-to-end transitions are not readable.
standouts: Strong human accountability boundary for consequential changes.
Blast-radius simulation plus staged change and rollback form a coherent safety workflow.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible operational value, with enough product evidence to warrant advancement despite missing video.

one_line: Agent-native storefront exposing shopping, cart, and checkout operations through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Lets an agent search and compare products, manage a cart, browse categories, and complete checkout on the same e-commerce site as a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured product and cart tools improve precision for multi-step shopping, but a capable general agent can achieve much of the same outcome through ordinary storefront interaction.
leverage_evidence: About text lists 12 tools spanning search, details, comparison, recommendations, cart management, checkout, history, and categories.
Example request is a constrained search followed by adding the cheapest matching item.
execution_rationale: A live demo and public repository support plausibility, but there is no video and the packet does not demonstrate checkout completion or error-state handling.
execution_evidence: FACTS report demo_alive=alive, public_repo=True, and six gallery images.
About text describes a complete tool set and a concrete shopping flow.
impact_rationale: Shopping agents have a clear audience and repetitive search/comparison/cart burden; the value is credible, though the store appears primarily demonstrative.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies the gap between recommendation chatbots and agents that can perform shopping actions.
Product covers discovery through purchase rather than only recommendations.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native commerce is a relevant and competent WebMCP application with a useful end-to-end angle, but the concept is a familiar category.
creativity_evidence: Frames or video are not submitted; originality is primarily evidenced by the described tool surface and same-site agent interaction.
usability_note: The described flows are familiar and likely approachable, but visual evidence is limited to packaging.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or transcript.
Checkout and purchase correctness are claimed rather than demonstrated.
standouts: Covers the full shopping loop with a concrete agent request example.
advance_reason: Clear WebMCP commerce use case and credible scope, though evidence is thinner than the strongest entries.

one_line: WebMCP shopping assistant for searching, comparing, reviewing, and cart management.
what_it_does: Registers structured shopping tools so an agent can search/filter products, inspect details and reviews, compare options, and manage a cart while the user watches updates.
leverage_rationale: Structured filters and shopping state make delegated comparison and cart work more reliable, but the same outcome is generally possible through UI automation with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text names 10 tools and structured search parameters including category, price range, and minimum rating.
Submission claims real-time UI updates as the agent acts.
execution_rationale: The live demo, public repository, and repeated screenshots indicate a coherent shopping UI, but no video or end-to-end proof limits the claimed completion score.
execution_evidence: FACTS report demo_alive=alive, public_repo=True, and four gallery images.
About text describes a consistent set of tools and real-time activity log.
impact_rationale: Product discovery and comparison are common, concrete shopping pain points, and the proposed personal-shopper workflow addresses them directly.
impact_evidence: Inspiration describes scrolling, cross-tab comparison, reviews, and coupon/search overload.
Tool list maps directly to search, comparison, reviews, and cart actions.
creativity_rationale: A competent agent-assisted shopping application with a useful angle, but the concept and interaction model are established.
creativity_evidence: Novelty is mainly the WebMCP integration and live activity presentation rather than a new shopping model.
usability_note: The visible activity-log and search screenshots suggest understandable feedback, though exact flow quality is not fully shown.
red_flags: Claims of fully functional tools are not independently demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Good mapping from structured filters to a practical delegated shopping workflow.
advance_reason: Useful and credible but comparatively conventional, with limited evidence for exceptional leverage or originality.

one_line: Shared expense ledger where natural-language input becomes precise participant-specific splits.
what_it_does: Maintains a shared group ledger, supports even/share/exact splits, shows balance explanations, computes settlements, and lets an agent add expenses from a sentence.
leverage_rationale: The agent removes the central data-entry bottleneck and can translate one ambiguous sentence into multiple correctly scoped expenses while sharing live ledger state; UI automation would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text gives a verified example producing three add_expense calls with different participant lists.
Ledger exposes 14 tools and provides line-by-line balance derivations and settlement calculations.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a tightly scoped complete workflow and video frame sheets support a real ledger UI, though no transcript/video is supplied for direct end-to-end observation.
execution_evidence: About text covers expense entry, participant-specific splits, balances, breakdowns, settlements, and agent interaction.
FACTS report a live demo and three frame sheets.
Gallery packaging screenshot is present.
impact_rationale: Group-travel and shared-expense reconciliation are concrete recurring problems; reducing the logging burden addresses why existing apps go unused.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies manual form entry and participant selection as the bottleneck.
Natural-language example handles missed participants and multiple payers.
creativity_rationale: The concept finds a strong, specific WebMCP fit in translating a messy sentence into structured financial records, with meaningful auditability rather than a generic chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Explicit framing of the bottleneck as data entry, not arithmetic.
Shared balance rail and explainable per-person breakdown reinforce the concept.
usability_note: The ledger, balances, and settlement panel are described as transparent and user-verifiable.
red_flags: Video transcript is absent, so the claimed verification cannot be independently checked from packet media.
standouts: Excellent concrete demonstration of heterogeneous participant lists from one natural-language request.
Balances are shown and explained rather than merely asserted.
advance_reason: Strong fit between WebMCP's structured actions and a real data-entry pain point, with credible product completeness.

one_line: Agent-native image forensics engine exposing structured evidence and reports.
what_it_does: Analyzes images for detection scores, metadata, noise, frequency-domain signals, and combined forensic reports, then exposes those results to agents for explanation.
leverage_rationale: Structured forensic evidence is more useful and reliable to an agent than scraping a visual report, especially for multi-signal explanation; the underlying analysis remains available without WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: About text distinguishes the application's forensic engine from the agent's explanatory role.
Six named tools expose analysis, scores, signals, metadata, frequency analysis, and reports.
execution_rationale: The architecture and tool boundaries are coherent, but only two gallery images and no video leave the actual analysis workflow and output quality largely unverified.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, public repository, and two gallery images.
About text specifies multiple forensic signals and a combined report.
impact_rationale: Image authenticity and provenance are real needs for investigators, journalists, and careful media consumers; structured evidence can improve explanations and auditability.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies difficulty evaluating images and lack of direct access to forensic evidence.
Product returns multiple concrete signal types rather than an unsupported binary label.
creativity_rationale: Combining a client-side forensic engine with agent-readable evidence is a fresh, technically meaningful application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Clear separation between deterministic forensic analysis and agent interpretation.
Frequency and noise evidence are more distinctive than generic image captioning.
usability_note: Potentially useful for investigation, but the packet does not show enough output detail to assess interpretability.
red_flags: Accuracy of forensic conclusions is not established by the packet.
standouts: Agent receives structured evidence from a purpose-built analysis engine rather than asking the agent to infer pixels alone.
advance_reason: Distinctive and credible concept with meaningful structured-evidence leverage, despite thin execution proof.

one_line: Local-first collaborative whiteboard where humans and agents make precise reversible canvas edits.
what_it_does: Extends an Excalidraw-like canvas with inspection, atomic patches, selective rollback, focus, visual capture, export, and scene import through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured canvas state, revision/epoch checks, selective rollback, and visual grounding create a collaboration model that ordinary UI-driving agents cannot replicate comparably reliably.
leverage_evidence: About text describes shared undo history, stale-write rejection, element IDs, atomic patches, and agent/human edits on one canvas.
Agent can inspect structure and visual context, prototype HTML, export, and revert only its own patch.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually detailed interaction contract and frame sheets show the product, although the absence of transcript limits direct proof of all workflows.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, two gallery images, and two frame sheets.
About text covers drawing, selection, correction, HTML prototypes, export, and selective rollback.
Described hard cases include arrow attachment, noisy pointer coalescing, and human-change protection.
impact_rationale: Designers, product teams, and prototypers can benefit from asking agents to make targeted canvas changes while retaining human control and editability.
impact_evidence: Concrete workflow: human circles a step, agent identifies it and makes a correction, then adds an interactive form.
Local-first and reversible semantics address trust and collaboration concerns.
creativity_rationale: The concept deeply pursues human-agent co-editing of a visual workspace, including structural grounding, visual capture, reversible patches, and sandboxed live prototypes.
creativity_evidence: Selective rollback that avoids clobbering later human work.
Canvas is both visual artifact and structured shared state.
Sandboxed HTML prototypes extend beyond static diagramming.
usability_note: Reversibility, focus, and readable element references are strong usability choices; full ergonomics are not fully visible.
red_flags: No transcript; some advanced flows remain claims rather than directly readable evidence.
standouts: Strong bridge between visual human intent and structured agent edits.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: WebMCP changes the interaction model itself and the concept is pursued with substantial technical depth.

one_line: Durable marketplace workspace where people and outside agents research, organize, and negotiate together.
what_it_does: Combines native and tracked outside listings with boards, alerts, research notebooks, comparisons, deal calculations, messages, offers, and human approval boundaries exposed through a large contextual WebMCP surface.
leverage_rationale: The product is built around persistent shared state between a human and an outside agent: contextual tool packs, durable canvas, cited research, approvals, and recorded decisions are difficult to reproduce through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript describes signed-out bootstrap tools, post-login rediscovery, persistent shared canvas, contextual marketplace packs, and approval-gated actions.
About text states 121 structured tools, durable agent findings, human notes, decisions, undo history, alerts, conversations, offers, and trade rooms.
Transcript explicitly says the site contains no embedded LLM and is designed for outside agents.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets evidence a broad but internally coherent marketplace/workspace with persistent state, dynamic tool exposure, and approval flows; scope is ambitious yet specifically articulated.
execution_evidence: FACTS report a 165-second live video, three frame sheets, public repository, and live demo.
Transcript walks through bootstrap, sign-in, browsing, boards, research, calculations, and approval-gated publishing/contact/offer/trade actions.
About text distinguishes native inventory from outside-listing snapshots.
impact_rationale: Collectors and buyers of vehicles, boats, campers, motorcycles, and machinery have real fragmented-search and negotiation problems; the shared research workspace offers credible value for this niche.
impact_evidence: About text identifies lost finds, rigid alerts, scattered research, and difficult multi-party trades.
Product supports cited research, inspection risks, acquisition cost, and offer planning.
creativity_rationale: A marketplace intentionally designed as a durable human-agent canvas, with outside-agent interoperability, contextual capability activation, and explicit verification boundaries, is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Outside agents rather than a built-in model are central to the concept.
Shared marketplace canvas and structured multi-party trade rooms extend beyond standard shopping assistants.
Dynamic contextual tool registration is used as a product mechanic.
usability_note: The transcript indicates clear separation between fluid research and explicit approval checkpoints; breadth may increase complexity.
red_flags: Requires sign-in for the full workspace, so accessibility depends on the demonstrated credential flow.
Very broad scope creates some risk of uneven depth across features.
standouts: Best evidence of an outside-agent, persistent human-agent collaboration model.
Approval boundary is explicit and auditable without suppressing exploratory work.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, strong video evidence, and exceptional ambition/originality make this a clear advancement candidate.

one_line: Cooperative escape-room game in which a human solves clues while an agent operates a changing space-station tool surface.
what_it_does: Presents a timed orbital-station puzzle with hidden dependencies, structured machine operations, state-dependent tool discovery, and a human physical override for final release.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is part of the game mechanic: structured discovery, validated actuation, state-dependent capabilities, and a human-only override create collaboration not well replicated by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text says available capabilities change as power and communications puzzles are solved.
Agent uses inspect_power_grid and schema-guided route_power rather than guessing controls.
Final emergency release requires a live human interface override.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused, coherent game loop and frame sheets provide product evidence, but no video or transcript means the timed end-to-end game is not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, two gallery images, and three frame sheets.
About text specifies a twelve-minute objective, system progression, consequences, and final gate.
impact_rationale: The intended audience is players seeking cooperative puzzle play; the human-agent division of strengths creates credible entertainment and experimentation value.
impact_evidence: Escape-room structure gives the human interpretation and judgment while the agent handles structured machinery.
Human-in-the-loop interaction is meaningful to the game outcome.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP discovery and changing tool availability as puzzle mechanics is a memorable, original interaction model rather than a game with an agent bolted on.
creativity_evidence: Capability discovery is itself part of progression.
Different strengths of human and agent are encoded into the puzzle design.
Timed physical authorization creates a distinctive finale.
usability_note: The bounded objective and explicit division of roles should be understandable, though timed coordination may be demanding.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; complete playthrough and polish are not verifiable.
Timed gameplay may depend on an agent environment not available to every user.
standouts: WebMCP discovery is integrated into the puzzle rather than hidden behind automation.
advance_reason: Highly creative and genuinely agent-native game concept with strong described leverage; advance pending limited execution evidence.

one_line: Mission-control graph where humans and a Codex fleet share state, permissions, approvals, and history through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect and modify a dependency graph, dispatch workers, expose contextual node tools, catch up via cursors/deltas, and operate under human-confirmed policies with auditable grants.
leverage_rationale: Persistent state, bounded deltas, contextual tool registration, policy-backed approval, and real worker dispatch make the page a shared mission surface rather than an automation target.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript demonstrates graph_digest, cursors, changes-since deltas, staged policy, human confirmation, dispatch, contextual node tools, and replay.
About text specifies session-bound grants, nonce use, capability references, and recorded approvals.
The page is explicitly the durable meeting point for agents working at different times.
execution_rationale: The 175-second video transcript and frame sheets describe and show a broad but coherent graph/agent workflow, including worker dispatch and approval safeguards.
execution_evidence: FACTS report a live 175-second video, three frame sheets, public repository, and live demo.
Transcript walks through digest, catch-up, approval, dispatch, node selection, split preview/application, and replay.
About text aligns with the transcript on graph state, deltas, grants, and auditability.
impact_rationale: Teams coordinating parallel agents need durable status, handoffs, approvals, and accountability; the product directly addresses loss of context and unsafe dispatch.
impact_evidence: About text identifies difficulty tracking who did what and why across parallel agents.
Product provides graph state, handoffs, decisions, policy-bound approvals, and replay.
creativity_rationale: The mission graph as a persistent human-agent control plane, with dynamic contextual tools and auditable capability grants, is an ambitious and original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Contextual node selection changes the exposed tool set.
Cursor-based catch-up and policy/nonce audit design are unusually deep for a hackathon product.
Real Codex worker dispatch ties the conceptual model to execution.
usability_note: The approval preview, graph canvas, and replay model support trust; the breadth of controls may require onboarding.
red_flags: Login and external worker infrastructure may limit reproducibility for evaluators.
Operational reliability of real fleet dispatch beyond the demo is not established.
standouts: Exceptional permission and audit model for agent actions.
Dynamic contextual WebMCP surface is product-defining, not decorative.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and strong direct evidence; this is a leading candidate for agent-infrastructure impact.

one_line: Missed-call rescue desk that turns an inbox into a cited, owner-approved reply plan without sending messages.
what_it_does: Compares fictional missed calls against owner capacity, stages a cited rescue plan, drafts editable replies, and requires the owner for acceptance, review, and any eventual send capability.
leverage_rationale: Cross-call comparison, exact citations, staged state, stale-edit protection, and capability separation give agents reliable preparation while preserving a human approval boundary; generic automation would be less safe and auditable.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five tools, cited plan staging, owner acceptance, draft revision, review queue, and explicit unavailable agent capabilities.
Caller text is marked untrusted and cannot create approval/review/send capabilities.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and internally coherent, with four frame sheets and a live demo, but no video means the full inbox-to-draft workflow remains claimed.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo, public repo, four gallery images, and three frame sheets.
About text specifies owner brief, capacity constraint, plan, accepted lead, draft revision, review, discard, and reset states.
impact_rationale: Small service-business owners have a concrete missed-call triage problem while occupied; cited prioritization and editable replies can save time without unsafe autonomous outreach.
impact_evidence: Inspiration gives a detailing-shop owner scenario and capacity-limited reply need.
Product addresses prioritization across deadline, job value, permissions, and owner capacity.
creativity_rationale: The rescue-desk framing and strict non-sending approval design are a thoughtful, specific CRM workflow rather than generic message drafting.
creativity_evidence: Nothing can send, and the agent cannot accept its own plan or approve a draft.
Stale edits cannot be queued, making workflow integrity part of the concept.
usability_note: Owner checkpoints and editable drafts provide clear control; the focused workflow should be approachable for a small business user.
red_flags: No video or transcript; end-to-end tool invocation is not directly observed.
Fictional inbox and limited domain scope constrain generality, though that is not a quality penalty.
standouts: Strong safety model: untrusted caller text cannot escalate authority.
Cited rescue plan bridges agent reasoning and owner accountability.
advance_reason: Concrete audience/problem fit and unusually careful approval semantics make this a strong, credible workflow even with incomplete media evidence.
